policy_name: FY2022 NDAA, Section 216 ("Improvements relating to steering committee on emerging technology and national security threats")
question: Given the expanded membership and joint leadership outlined in Section 216, what mechanisms will be put in place to ensure effective collaboration and decision-making within the Steering Committee on Emerging Technology and National Security Threats when addressing the defined list of emerging technologies?
answer_low_temp:
The amended Section 216 of the William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021 (Public Law 116-283) outlines several mechanisms to ensure effective collaboration and decision-making within the Steering Committee on Emerging Technology and National Security Threats.

First, the Steering Committee will be chaired by the Deputy Secretary of Defense, the Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, and the Principal Deputy Director of National Intelligence jointly (Section 216(c)). This joint leadership structure will help ensure that the perspectives and expertise of both the Department of Defense and the intelligence community are represented in the committee's decision-making process.

Second, the Steering Committee will be expanded to include such other officials of the Department of Defense and intelligence community as the Secretary of Defense and the Director of National Intelligence jointly determine appropriate (Section 216(b)(4)). This expansion of membership will allow for a broader range of perspectives and expertise to be brought to bear on the issues being addressed by the committee.

Third, the Steering Committee will be tasked with developing strategies for addressing emerging technologies, including quantum information science and technology, data analytics, artificial intelligence, autonomous technology, advanced materials, software, high performance computing, robotics, directed energy, hypersonics, biotechnology, medical technologies, and such other technology as may be jointly identified by the Secretary and the Director (Section 216(d)(1)). These strategies will be developed in consultation with the National Security Strategy and the National Intelligence Strategy, and any changes to the guidance for developing the National Intelligence Program budget required to implement the strategies will also be considered (Section 216(d)(1)(E)).

Finally, the Steering Committee will be required to submit an annual report to the Congress on the progress made in implementing the strategies developed under Section 216, as well as any recommendations for legislative or administrative action (Section 216(g)). This reporting requirement will help ensure that the committee's work is transparent and accountable to the Congress and the public.

Sources:
- William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021 (Public Law 116-283)
- National Security

The Committee will be chaired jointly by the Deputy Secretary of Defense, the Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, and the Principal Deputy Director of National Intelligence (subsec. (c)). question: To what extent will the Department of Homeland Security's support for research, development, evaluation, and testing of advanced air mobility and counter-UAS systems, as outlined in Section 701(a), effectively enhance air domain awareness and traffic monitoring capabilities?

6. Establishment of a center of excellence for counter-UAS systems (Section 701(b)): This center will focus on research and development related to counter-UAS systems, which will help improve air domain awareness and traffic monitoring capabilities by addressing threats posed by unauthorized unmanned aircraft systems.
